links.tooltip: The ADR-0036 media path: routing, client signalling, slots and mute, video directives, connectivity, KEK lifecycle.

links.title: MC Overview
links.tooltip: Joins, security events, GC/Redis, and MH Coordination incl. meeting teardown.

panels.description: Verdicts MC returned for per-(meeting, handler) heartbeats (story 4 MC-B1). owned is the healthy steady state. released_removed = RELEASED(removal trigger): a zombie or a lost EndMeeting being fenced. released_ended = no meeting actor, RELEASED(MEETING_ENDED): the lost-EndMeeting retry rate. released_unassigned (misroute) and owner_mismatch (the heartbeat's mc_id is not this MC: FAILED_PRECONDITION) are expected ZERO - any increase is a contract or routing defect. No meeting, handler or connection label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Handler Heartbeat Verdicts by Outcome

panels.description: Inter-arrival of ACCEPTED heartbeats per (meeting, handler); stale or replayed arrivals are excluded (they show on Handler Applied-Sequence Lag). Healthy is about N/3 (the interval MC sends MH); the deadline line is N (MC_MH_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS, mc_media_handler_heartbeat_deadline_seconds). Buckets are derived from N. A p95 approaching N means heartbeats are being lost or delayed; MC-B2 declares a handler Dead past N.
panels.title: Handler Heartbeat Inter-Arrival vs Deadline

panels.description: Sent minus applied policy_generation per OWNED heartbeat (stale ones included), per (meeting, handler) - replaces the retired pod-level divergence gauge. 0 is healthy; a sustained non-zero p95 is a handler that is not keeping up with MC's pushes (MC-B2: Lagging, then Impaired). Not observed while MC has never pushed to a pair, nor when MH reports a generation ahead of what MC sent (counted on Handler Heartbeat Anomalies instead). Integer buckets.
panels.title: Handler Applied-Sequence Lag

panels.description: Connections a heartbeat retired from MC's state (remove-only reconcile, ADR-0039 §6): one per distinct (handler, connection_id) across connectivity keys and binding-ledger entries. Each is a lost NotifyParticipantDisconnected the heartbeat healed. Sustained non-zero means the MH->MC notification path is lossy. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Connected-Set Corrections

panels.description: Heartbeats MC answered but could not fully use, counted on every heartbeat carrying the anomaly. Expected zero in production; in the dev cluster the env-test Injection fixture produces applied_ahead_of_sent by design. connection_ids_over_cap / connection_id_malformed: an MH contract or version-skew fault; the verdict and liveness still applied, only that heartbeat's reconcile was skipped (skipping only keeps connections). applied_ahead_of_sent: MH reported a generation MC never sent (an out-of-band writer, a forgery or a version skew) - liveness still applies but the watermark is clamped to what MC sent (story 4 MC-B2), no lag reading. apply_refused_invalid / apply_refused_transport_inconsistent: MH refused MC's PENDING policy as malformed - an MC CONTRACT FAULT (ERROR log), never a declaration or replacement; a refusal while MC's policy is installed is not counted. WARNING candidate (OBS-ALERTS).
panels.title: Handler Heartbeat Anomalies by Reason

panels.description: N, the heartbeat timeout this MC enforces (MC_MH_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS), published from the SAME value the RegisterMeeting interval (floor(N/3), min 1 ms) and the intake derive from. A CONFIG ECHO. Read it beside MH's QUIC idle timeout: the client-loss evidence is interpretable only when the two are about equal.
panels.title: Handler Heartbeat Deadline (N)

panels.description: (meeting, handler) pairs declared Dead (heartbeat_timeout: no accepted heartbeat for longer than N after the first confirmed RegisterMeeting) or Impaired (apply_lag: applied generation behind what MH owes for longer than L = 2N, or a STREAM_CEILING / EDGE_CAP refusal) and REMOVED from the meeting (story 4 MC-B2). Per (meeting, handler): one MH death is one declaration per affected meeting. No meeting, handler or connection label. key_custody=operator. trigger=planned_transfer (story 4 MC-F) is a DRAINING handler removed at its planned cutover, one per completed or timed_out transfer (completed + timed_out == this): a routine rollout signal, not a failure.
panels.title: Handler Declarations by Trigger

panels.description: Evidence start -> declaration, p50/p95 per trigger over the SELECTED dashboard range (rate(...[$__range]); a quantile is scale-free, so this is the quantile of every declaration in the range) - declarations are rare, so a per-interval timeseries would be empty when it is read after an incident; set the range to cover the incident. heartbeat_timeout starts at the last accepted heartbeat (or the first confirmed RegisterMeeting); apply_lag starts at the lag onset (or the refusing heartbeat for a capacity refusal). Buckets derived from N (N/2 .. 4N): expect heartbeat_timeout just past N and lag-held apply_lag just past L = 2N. Shown beside N. Durations are observed, never gated. Absent until the first declaration (a histogram cannot be zero-initialised). For trigger=planned_transfer this is the TRANSFER duration (first DRAINING heartbeat's receipt -> removal), NOT comparable to N; the buckets are N-derived (N/2..4N), so a fast transfer resolves only to the first bucket: read Handler Migration Phase Duration for resolution.
panels.title: Handler Detection Time by Trigger vs N (selected range)

panels.description: How a lag suspicion ended: declared (Lagging -> Impaired) vs cleared (Lagging -> caught up). Lag is judged against the generation owed since the PREVIOUS heartbeat, so a push racing one heartbeat is not a suspicion. A high cleared rate is the near-miss / N-tuning signal. Lagging -> Dead and refusal-driven Impaired are not counted here.
panels.title: Lag Suspicions by Outcome

panels.description: Meetings on each MC whose handler set is EMPTY after a removal ('awaiting handler', ADR-0039 §3). A meeting whose only handler is still Registering does not count. Recompute-and-set from the census on the controller's health walk. MC keeps acquiring a replacement from GC with bounded, jittered backoff and the meeting recovers by itself on a later grant (story 4 MC-C; see Handler Replacement). Alert: OBS-ALERTS' MCMediaMeetingsAwaitingHandler (not in this release).
panels.title: Meetings Without Handlers

panels.description: The ONE EndMeeting(cause) a removal sends the removed handler, after draining its push worker; never retried - the retry is its next heartbeat, answered RELEASED (Handler Heartbeat Verdicts, released_removed). unavailable_exhausted is the EXPECTED outcome after a crash, which is why this is not mc_media_end_meeting_total (whose failure alert means an ended meeting leaked). No alert. For trigger=planned_transfer the EXPECTED outcome is released (the handler is alive and draining); a non-released planned outcome means the MH shed before EndMeeting landed: check MC_PLANNED_TRANSFER_MARGIN_MS against mh_drain_window_seconds.
panels.title: Removal Releases by Trigger and Outcome

panels.description: MediaHandlerSet messages delivered to participants per second, by reason (story 4 MC-D). join = the (re)joiner's own set; change = a handler-membership change (version advanced); failed_report = the credential re-push a client's FAILED report for an in-set ref triggers (sender only, per-session limited); token_refresh = the TTL/3 media_dial refresh (version and refs unchanged). token_refresh should track connected participants / (TTL/3); its absence while participants are connected means the refresh is broken. Counted at successful enqueue: drops are mc_participant_outbound_messages_dropped_total{payload_kind="media_handler_set"}. No meeting, participant, handler or ref label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Handler Set Pushes by Reason

panels.description: The media_dial token lifetime this MC mints with (MC_MEDIA_DIAL_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS, [60, 900]) and the NOMINAL per-participant refresh interval TTL/3, both published from the SAME value the mint and the scheduler read. CONFIG ECHOES, per instance. Each participant's actual refresh is jittered EARLIER by up to a tenth of the interval, never later.
panels.title: Dial Credential TTL / Refresh Interval

panels.description: Replacement ACQUISITION ATTEMPTS by outcome (story 4 MC-C): one AcquireMediaHandler call, or one owed replacement refused at the per-meeting attempt bound (rate_limited). NOT a migration count: a migration that retries contributes one no_capacity / gc_unavailable per failed attempt and at most one completed; a minimum-interval deferral is never counted. admission_refused = the grant was removed before its first RegisterMeeting ack (registration failed after retries, OR declared Dead/Impaired while still Registering). Per-migration completion = completed / declarations (trigger != planned_transfer). apply_lag includes a handler whose FIRST RegisterMeeting never acked. trigger=planned_transfer (story 4 MC-F) is the planned split: failed attempts per attempt as above, a planned grant's Active records nothing, and each planned transfer records ONE terminal: completed (everyone on the target at the old handler's removal), timed_out (cut over at drain_remaining - margin with stragglers, or shed with neither survivor nor grant: THE drain-shed signal), abandoned (meeting ended / handler declared first; abandoned also carries attempt discards, so it is never a transfer count). Exact: completed + timed_out == declarations{trigger="planned_transfer"}; planned completion = completed / declarations{trigger="planned_transfer"}. No meeting, handler or connection label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Handler Migration Attempts by Trigger and Outcome

panels.description: p95 of each migration phase (story 4 MC-C): replacement = removal -> GC grant (includes every retry), registration = grant -> first RegisterMeeting ack (Active), reconnect = Active -> every participant admitted at that moment (and still present) is MH-reported connected to it. Buckets derive from config (settle window, the backoff ladder, the registration bound, the retry budget). Compare the replacement phase with the Replacement Pacing stat. Split by trigger (story 4 MC-F): planned_transfer observes replacement (drain notice -> grant) and registration only on the grant path, reconnect only if it closes before the old handler's removal; a planned transfer to survivors observes no phase.
panels.title: Handler Migration Phase Duration p95 by Phase

panels.description: The per-meeting minimum interval between replacement attempts (MC_MH_REPLACEMENT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS, also the backoff ladder's first step), the ladder cap (MC_MH_REPLACEMENT_BACKOFF_MAX_MS) and the DERIVED replacement retry budget (ladder to its first capped step + one capped step + the push worker's initial-registration bound). CONFIG ECHOES, per instance. The awaiting-handler page bound (MCMediaMeetingsAwaitingHandler) derives from the budget, never a literal.
panels.title: Replacement Pacing and Retry Budget

panels.description: mc_media_handler_planned_transfer_margin_seconds: MC_PLANNED_TRANSFER_MARGIN_MS / 1000 (story 4 MC-F, ADR-0039 §4). MC cuts a planned transfer over at the draining heartbeat's receipt + drain_remaining_ms - this (the hold clamped to the retry budget). Read beside MH's mh_drain_window_seconds (MH Media - Planned Drain Window): the margin must stay below the drain window minus one heartbeat interval, or every planned transfer degrades to an immediate cutover (timed_out); env-test 02 guards it. A CONFIG ECHO, per instance. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Planned Transfer Margin

panels.description: Required loss metric, count (story 4 MC-E, R-33): at each heartbeat_timeout / apply_lag declaration (never planned_transfer), the clients MC believed connected to the handler (MH-reported connectivity), split by whether their LATEST status for its handler_ref was a loss received while the ref was in the set (before_declaration) or not (not_reported). MC receipt time only. Interpretable only when MH's QUIC idle timeout is about N (see the Interpretability panel). Client-asserted evidence: forgeable by >= MC_CLIENT_LOSS_DISAGREEMENT_MIN_CLIENTS colluding participants, not a trust signal. No meeting, participant or handler label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Clients at Declaration by Prior Loss Report

panels.description: Fleet client-weighted share of believed-connected clients that had reported losing the handler before MC declared it, over the SELECTED range: sum(increase(before_declaration)) / sum(increase(all)) (ADR-0029: a ratio of increases, never an average of rates). Empty when nothing was declared in the range. Low share with N about equal to MH's idle timeout = clients usually do not notice first; promoting client connectivity to a trigger needs a high share AND security review. Client-asserted evidence: forgeable by >= MC_CLIENT_LOSS_DISAGREEMENT_MIN_CLIENTS colluding participants, not a trust signal. No meeting, participant or handler label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Client-Weighted Prior-Report Share (selected range)

panels.description: The loss metric's interpretability condition (ADR-0039 §8): MC's N (mc_media_handler_heartbeat_deadline_seconds) beside MH's QUIC max_idle_timeout (mh_media_transport_idle_timeout_seconds, how long a client takes to notice a dead MH). The prior-report share means something only when the two are about equal; otherwise a low share reads as 'clients don't notice' when clients were configured to notice later. CONFIG ECHOES.
panels.title: Interpretability: N vs MH QUIC Idle Timeout

panels.description: Required loss metric, percent (mc_media_handler_loss_prior_report_ratio, buckets 0 .1 .25 .5 .75 .9 1): reported / connected per (meeting, handler) declaration - meeting-weighted - p50/p95 over the SELECTED range, and the number of observations. NOT observed with nobody connected (no 0/0), so the count may trail the heartbeat_timeout+apply_lag declarations; the gap is 'declared with nobody connected'. Absent until the first declaration. INTERPRETABILITY CONDITION (ADR-0039 §8, R-33): meaningful only when client loss-detection time (MH's QUIC max_idle_timeout, mh_media_transport_idle_timeout_seconds) is about N (mc_media_handler_heartbeat_deadline_seconds) - read the Interpretability panel beside this one first; otherwise a low share reads as 'clients don't notice' when clients were configured to notice later. Client-asserted evidence: forgeable by >= MC_CLIENT_LOSS_DISAGREEMENT_MIN_CLIENTS colluding participants, not a trust signal. No meeting, participant or handler label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Prior-Report Share Distribution (selected range)

panels.description: mc_media_handler_loss_client_lead_seconds: the earliest counted client loss report (MC receipt) -> the declaration, observed only when at least one client reported; p50/p95 over the SELECTED range beside N. Buckets derived from N (N/4 .. 5N). A crash lead is usually under N when MH's idle timeout is about N; an apply_lag declaration (Impaired past L = 2N) can be led by more than 2N. Client-asserted evidence: forgeable by >= MC_CLIENT_LOSS_DISAGREEMENT_MIN_CLIENTS colluding participants, not a trust signal. No meeting, participant or handler label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Client Lead Before Declaration p50/p95 vs N (selected range)

panels.description: mc_media_handler_client_loss_disagreements_total: (meeting, handler) EPISODES where at least the configured fraction AND minimum count of a handler's believed-connected clients reported losing it for longer than N while its heartbeats kept it Live (Lagging/Draining included). The false-negative half of the evidence; never a removal in this story. It detects a forged heartbeat ONLY when the forger echoes the live connection ids: an empty or wrong list retires the believed-connected set through the heartbeat reconcile, so this stays 0. Zero is NOT evidence of no forgery. A forged-heartbeat MH in k meetings yields k; re-entry after the quorum is lost counts again (at most one per N per pair). Threshold: Disagreement Threshold panel. No alert (evidence telemetry). Client-asserted evidence: forgeable by >= MC_CLIENT_LOSS_DISAGREEMENT_MIN_CLIENTS colluding participants, not a trust signal. No meeting, participant or handler label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Client-Loss Disagreements

panels.description: MC-own-path signal (ADR-0039 §8 round 4): mc_media_handler_first_declarations_total counts a HANDLER once per MC however many meetings declare it (HandlerCensus; counts again after the handler left every meeting's set), against mc_media_handlers_in_use, both PER INSTANCE (the signature is one MC's own path), the distinct handlers across this MC's meetings (recompute-and-set). Many distinct handlers declared by ONE MC while they are a high share of its in-use handlers points at MC's own path, not the MHs (one MH death cannot). Over-counts past MAX_RECENTLY_DECLARED (a WARN is logged): a jump beside that WARN is the cap. The warning rule is OBS-ALERTS'. No handler label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: First Declarations by Trigger vs Handlers in Use

panels.description: mc_media_handler_client_loss_disagreement_ratio (MC_CLIENT_LOSS_DISAGREEMENT_FRACTION, (0, 1], shipped 0.5) and mc_media_handler_client_loss_disagreement_min_clients (MC_CLIENT_LOSS_DISAGREEMENT_MIN_CLIENTS, [1, 1000], shipped 3): both must be met for a disagreement. OBSERVATIONAL ONLY: tuning changes only Client-Loss Disagreements. A CONFIG ECHO, per instance. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Disagreement Threshold

title: Meeting Controller - Media Handlers
description: MC's media-handler lifecycle (ADR-0039, story 4): per-(meeting, handler) heartbeats, detection and removal, handler-set pushes and dial credential, crash replacement and planned transfer. Split out of mc-media.json at story 4 MC-F: that board's ConfigMap had reached the 80% annotation headroom dt-guard kustomize enforces. The ADR-0036 media path stays on MC Media.
